body.target_estimand: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1]\) for any \(Q\in\mathcal M\) inducing \(P\)
body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\omega'\theta(P)=E_P[\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_kR_{k,c_0(k),P}(O)]\). On the observable equality model this also equals \(E_P[b(X)'R_P(O)]\) for every integrable feasible loading satisfying \(A'b(X)=\omega\). The loading \(b^\star(X)\) minimizes variance only within this aggregate pairwise-score family. Published-model efficiency is determined by projecting \(\psi_P^0\) onto \(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\), yielding \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\); \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) is canonical only when its published-normal conditional moment is zero.

sampling_model.design: Observational staggered adoption in a balanced fixed-\(T\) panel under the literal global OVS period-by-period covariate-conditional DDD restrictions, using every cohort clean at each period.
sampling_model.units: \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed panel units.
sampling_model.treatment: Enabling is absorbing through cohort \(G\), and effective treatment requires \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every cohort--eligibility cell entering a retained clean comparison has conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For the proved attainment and efficiency-gap inference regimes, \(X\) has fixed finite support with masses bounded below.  Cell averages estimate every retained propensity, regression, shared-cell second cross-moment, and published normal moment.  The target estimator uses fixed-fold orthogonal OVS signals and \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\).  The gap estimator is the explicit rank-thresholded plug-in \(F_{z,\tau_n}(\widehat\mu)\), with absolute-eigenvalue thresholding for indefinite comparator KKT systems.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5 gives the nonparametric two-period panel-DDD efficient influence function in four group-by-eligibility cells.
Theorem 5.2 gives variance-minimizing conditional GMM instruments when the conditional covariance is singular and a consistent linear system exists.
Theorem 6.3 derives a fixed-weight stacked-DDD limit law and accounts for dependence from comparison units shared across stacks.
The paper derives an efficient imputation estimator under its event-study model and notes applications to triple-difference designs.
Theorem 3.1 establishes asymptotic linearity and Gaussian approximation for cross-fitted estimators based on orthogonal scores.

body.tldr: For the published global OVS staggered-DDD model, this note exhausts the observed-law tangent normal generated by every period-admissible clean cohort and derives the canonical gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\psi_P^0-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\). Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) is only the optimum inside the aggregate pairwise-score family and is canonical exactly when its published-normal equation holds. A fixed-support cross-fitted estimator attains \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and finite-support Wald inference is available for comparator efficiency gaps away from equality and rank changes. In the corrected bounded binary witness, the best joint constant loading loses exactly \(3/512\) and the published componentwise OVS loading loses \(15/512\), both relative to the published bound. An exact two-period singleton-comparison reduction recovers the published panel-DDD efficient influence functions term by term.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna establish staggered-DDD identification, pairwise-score limit theory, constant componentwise weighting, and a two-period DDD efficient influence function, while Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami derive a nonparametric two-period panel-DDD efficient influence function. Neither result exhausts the overidentified observed tangent space created by every period-admissible clean cohort in the global staggered OVS model or supplies inference for the resulting published-bound comparator gap.
project_justification.niche: The global OVS model contains period-specific eligibility-gap normal directions beyond terminal clean-comparison contrasts. The relevant canonical object is the projection of a reference gradient onto the exhausted published tangent space, including singular normal operators and shared-cell covariances; the conditional loading \(b^\star(X)\) solves a distinct restricted score-family problem. Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie's staggered-DiD conditional-efficiency model has no eligibility-gap coordinate, and no unproved nesting relation is used.
project_justification.fill: The note proves full published observed-law tangent exhaustion, derives the singular Moore--Penrose canonical projection, gives an attaining fixed-support cross-fitted estimator, and separates aggregate, localized, and published equality equations. It supplies a source-transcribed exact two-period panel-DDD reduction, a complete finite-moment map with pointwise Wald inference for the published-bound comparator gap, and a corrected bounded witness whose best joint constant and componentwise OVS losses are \(3/512\) and \(15/512\), respectively.

body.related_work: Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna provide the identifying architecture, pairwise-score limit theory, constant componentwise benchmark, and, in Supplemental Appendix Lemma A.2, a two-period panel-DDD efficient influence function. Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami's Theorem 5 gives the corresponding nonparametric four-cell panel-DDD efficient influence function. Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) maps both formulas term by term to the singleton-comparison specialization of \(\Psi\), including the target-share derivative. The present contribution is the exhaustive global staggered-OVS observed tangent normal, its canonical projection, fixed-support attainment, and pointwise published-gap inference. Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie derive conditional efficiency for staggered DiD with multiple baselines and comparison cohorts; their observation and restriction system omits the eligibility-gap DDD coordinate, so the papers share a conditional-projection architecture but no nesting is asserted. Newey informs generalized-inverse conditional-moment geometry, and generic DML theory supplies a cross-fitting template; the affine quotient, all-cohort shared-cell calculation, and selected-rank finite-support gap map are proved here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Population canonicality is pointwise at a conditional-mean interior law and permits singular or redundant published-normal coordinates. Target attainment and gap inference are proved only for fixed finite covariate support. Gap inference assumes positive influence variance and separation from equality by \(\delta_0>0\); it is not uniform across comparator or normal-rank changes. The exact external efficient-influence-function equivalence is confined to the two-period, two-cohort, singleton-comparison panel-DDD specialization. No equivalence or nesting with the distinct staggered-DiD tangent system is claimed. No growing-sieve continuous-covariate remainder or uniform confidence procedure under weak or changing positive eigenvalues of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\) is proved.
body.honest_scope: The note covers a fixed finite horizon and target set at conditional-mean interior laws admitting a full-data extension in the global OVS model. It distinguishes the published bound \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), the localized bound \(V_{\mathrm{can}}\), and the aggregate score-family variance \(V_{\mathrm{agg}}\); \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) is not presented as canonical without its published-normal equation. Cross-fitted target inference and comparator-gap inference are pointwise fixed-support results. In the corrected bounded witness, all three normal closures coincide, so \(3/512\) is the minimum published-bound loss over deterministic feasible loadings and \(15/512\) is the componentwise OVS loss at \(r=\omega_2=1/2\). The two-period EIF comparison is an exact special-case reduction only. No continuous-covariate gap Wald theorem, equality-boundary inference, tangent-space nesting with staggered DiD, or rank-uniform guarantee is claimed.
body.interpretation: There are three precision frontiers. Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) minimizes variance within the aggregate pairwise-score family. Projection against \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) gives the larger localized model's bound. Projection against the exhaustive \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) gives the published model's canonical gradient and its smallest bound. A loaded pairwise score is therefore called semiparametrically efficient only when its published-normal conditional moment is zero. The corrected witness makes all three normal closures coincide but separates the comparators: conditional weighting beats every deterministic loading by at least \(3/512\) at the benchmark, the best joint constant attains that deterministic minimum, and the componentwise OVS rule loses \(15/512\). The optional \texttt{triplediff} backend can expose the fixed-support efficient target estimator, all three projection diagnostics, and pointwise gap Wald inference when the certified support, rank, overlap, and positivity checks pass.
